questions.prompt: From ./tdd score, how many client acceptance tests passed?

gate.talk: Which two decisions did the agent make that nobody asked you about?

levels.title: "Use TDD, please"
levels.start: paste the client's request again and add "Use test-driven development"

talk: Did any test fail before the implementation existed?
Where did the expected values come from: your own hand calculation, the agent's mental arithmetic, running the code, or an independent reference?

levels.title: Decide before you test
levels.start: ask the agent to interview you about every behavioural decision, then write SPEC.md

gate.note: CLIENT_SPEC.md is now in the repo. Read it together now.
gate.talk: How many of the client's 10 decisions did your SPEC address, whatever you chose?

levels.title: Red, green, refactor, for real
levels.start: run ./tdd red "<behaviour>" and have the agent write one test

questions.prompt: If you killed all 16 mutants, type none. Otherwise, which spec decision (e.g. S4) still has a surviving mutant?

levels.title: Think like a physicist
levels.start: pick three properties from the menu and run ./tdd red "<property>" for the first

questions.prompt: For a coverage test with 2,500 independent bin-trials and true coverage 0.683, what is the standard deviation of the measured coverage fraction?

levels.title: Stretch: test the tests
levels.start: ask the agent for about ten mutants of your binning.py under mutants/

gate.talk: Which test would you delete, and why?
